options.text: $XZ$ is the hypotenuse opposite the right angle, so $9^{2}+12^{2}=XZ^{2}$ and $XZ=15$.
Apply $9^{2}+12^{2}=XZ^{2}$ even when the right-angle mark at $Y$ is removed.
Writing $9^{2}+12^{2}=XZ^{2}$ forces the right angle at $Y$ into place.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Alok has $\triangle XYZ$ with a right angle at $Y$, $XY=9$, and $YZ=12$. He wants the length of $XZ$.

part_answers.answer: With a right angle at $Y$, the hypotenuse is $XZ$ opposite $Y$, so $9^{2}+12^{2}=XZ^{2}$ and $XZ=15$.

teacher.key_rationale: Right at Y → hypotenuse XZ; 81+144=225=15^2. B omits right-angle condition. C reverses. D misidentifies the hypotenuse.
